for_davis: Exam-first read: METR's 1.9x finding is the governance-and-safety story CCAR-P tests — AI accelerating its own R&D is the risk case behind the exam's governance domain. Claude reading bank accounts is the trust-and-permissions pattern his Life Time agent will need, and GPT-6 Cyber's gated rollout shows how the labs price and gate powerful models.
headline: GPT-6 Cyber goes gated, Claude reads your bank, and AI is now building AI twice as fast

stories.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber on Nov 5, a specialized model for vulnerability discovery and exploit research, initially available only to selected customers approved for its Daybreak Red program. The company says researchers using it reproduced 1,724 Linux kernel vulnerabilities, developed working exploits for 948, and found 81 previously unknown high-severity vulnerabilities in Firefox. API pricing is $20 per million input tokens and $100 output, 60% and 33% above its GPT-5.6 Cyber predecessor and well above rival cyber models from Anthropic and Google.
stories.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber: a security model that finds real vulnerabilities, gated behind approval
stories.why_it_matters: Security models are now a priced, gated product line, not a research demo — and the labs are competing on who finds real bugs while respecting researcher-set boundaries.

stories.summary: Google DeepMind said Nov 5 that Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, its video generation model, is generally available on the Gemini API and Gemini for business. Clips now run up to 15 seconds, up from 10, with improved scene consistency, character speech and multi-turn conversational editing, and 720p video costs $0.07 per second, 30% below the prior version. It is also available in the Gemini app, AI Studio, OpenRouter and Runway.
stories.title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash goes generally available: 15-second clips, 30% cheaper
stories.why_it_matters: Video generation keeps getting longer and cheaper at the same time — the cost curve that turns AI video from a demo into a tool a solo builder can actually ship with.

stories.summary: Anthropic announced Personal Finance in Claude on Nov 5, a beta rolling out to Pro, Max and Ultra subscribers in the US. Users link bank, card, loan and investment accounts through Plaid — up to 16 banks — and ask Claude about balances, spending and bills in plain language. Access is read-only: Claude cannot move, manage or invest money, and chats in the Personal Finance hub are not used for model training. It reads up to 24 months of transactions; investment and loan accounts expose balances and limits only, not holdings or terms.
stories.title: Anthropic launches Personal Finance in Claude: read-only bank access via Plaid, US beta
stories.why_it_matters: The assistant is becoming a trusted reader of private data, not just a chatbot — the permission and trust design here is the pattern every serious agent product will have to copy.

stories.summary: Independent evaluator METR published an 11-week assessment on Nov 5 after examining Anthropic's internal data: benchmark scores (AECI) have grown about 1.9x faster since October 2025 than before — roughly two years of historical progress in one year — and METR estimates perhaps 80% of the acceleration is due to AI itself, though with high uncertainty. Anthropic redacted most of the evidence METR found most informative, and METR called Anthropic's claim that it has not crossed its own 2x acceleration threshold 'overstated', saying crossing by July 15 was plausible.
stories.title: METR: Anthropic's models are improving 1.9x faster, and AI is doing much of the R&D
stories.why_it_matters: This is the clearest evidence yet of recursive self-improvement in practice — and the governance debate around it is exactly the CCAR-P safety and risk domain.

stories.summary: Thinking Machines Lab is set to close a fresh funding round as soon as this week, raising $5B led by Accel at a $40B pre-money valuation, more than tripling its valuation from its last public round last year, according to Business Insider. The raise follows a year in which the lab's models have shown up inside other companies' products — its Inkling-Small powers Cognition's new SWE-2 Flash coding agent.
stories.title: Thinking Machines Lab reportedly raising $5B at a $40B valuation
stories.why_it_matters: The lab that builds models for other builders is now valued like a frontier lab — a reminder that the picks-and-shovels layer of the AI stack is where the biggest checks are landing.

tldr: OpenAI launched GPT-6 Cyber for approved security teams, Google made Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generally available with 15-second clips at 30% less, and Anthropic rolled out a read-only Personal Finance beta in Claude via Plaid. METR's independent assessment found Anthropic's models improving 1.9x faster since October 2025, largely because AI is doing the R&D, and Thinking Machines Lab is reportedly raising $5B at a $40B valuation.
